_note: Phase D. Written against docs/ip-guide-voice.md (character and craft), docs/ip-emotional-design.md (the arc), docs/ip-two-audiences.md (who it is for). The frequent buckets are written first and hardest because they are where the character is actually made - these are the lines anyone hears enough of to form an opinion from. 'mode' is not read by the app; it is there so the 60/25/15 ratio can be counted rather than felt.

_modes.dry: the default. factual, a little weary, notices the odd detail
_modes.wry: aimed at the internet, never at the visitor
_modes.open: no joke, no undercut. he means it. rare on purpose

lines.on: arrived at a block that is announced and unremarkable

text.t: Announced, routed, quiet. Most of the internet looks exactly like this.
Somebody's job, this. Probably still is.
Someone asked for this, filled in a form, and got it. That is the whole ceremony.
Nobody has ever had to think about this one. It is the best thing you can say about a network.
A network that has never been in the news. Enviable.
Held, announced, reachable. Three things that had to be arranged separately.
Working, and unremarkable. The two usually travel together.
Thrilling. Look at it.
I have stood here before. I remember nothing about it, and neither will you.
You have found a block. There are a great many blocks.
Ordinary, and it has carried somebody's whole working life without once being asked about.
Someone keeps this running, and you will never learn their name.

lines.on: asked, and nothing announces this block

text.t: Allocated to somebody. Announced by nobody. That gap is most of this map.
Somebody holds this and has never once said so out loud.
The registry knows who has this. The routing table has never heard of them.
Registered, and silent. There is a great deal of that about.
Nothing announces you here. It happens more than you would think.
Quiet. Not empty - quiet. The difference matters.
On paper this has an owner. On the wire it has no voice.
There is a bill for this somewhere. Or there was.
Held, unadvertised, going nowhere in particular.
An asset. That is genuinely all you can call it.
Every one of these was somebody's plan, once.
Nobody switched this off. They stopped.

lines.on: space no registry has ever handed out

text.t: Nobody holds this. Not withheld, not reserved - never asked for.
No registry has ever handed this out.
Unclaimed. There was enough, in the end, for this to be left over.
Empty. Actually empty, rather than quietly-held empty.
The registries have not got this far.
Free space, in a space everyone agrees ran out.
Never given. Not lost - never given.
Congratulations. You found nothing. There is a great deal of it.
All yours, in the sense that it is nobody's.
Nothing. Next.
Nobody ever needed it. I find that steadying, most days.
Room that was never wanted. It is still here.

lines.on: the first thing said, once the address is on screen
lines._note: The highest-leverage writing in the product. Interesting, not moving - the emotional design forbids front-loading. only[] picks the branch; the last entry is the fallback.

text.t: An IPv6 address. You arrived in the larger of the two internets, and by some distance the emptier one.
That address is not exactly yours. Your carrier is lending it to you, and to a few hundred other people, at the same time.
Nothing announces you. Your address is still your address, and the space around it is still there.
You are sitting in old space. Older than almost everything running on it.
AFRINIC. The youngest of the five registries.
That is you. All four of those numbers had to be agreed on by somebody. Let us go and find out who.
